verdict: the 164 % case REPRODUCES on my build (got 163.7 % at N=250000, total 659130) and is deterministic across two runs.
on "unbounded in proportion": the sweep gives 3 distinct bands over 7 budgets, with
overshoot 19.4 % to 163.7 %. The overshoot is ONE FINAL ITERATION's node count, so it grows
with the position's branching at that depth rather than with N — which is why the PERCENTAGE
is largest at small/medium N and falls as N rises, not the other way round. It is bounded
absolutely by the 4N cap; it is not bounded as a percentage of N.
HARNESS CONSEQUENCE (one line): a harness that trusts the last reported count must also record
that the ABORTED iteration's nodes are NOT included, so any cost comparison between two
engines must add the same allowance on both sides or it will mis-price the cheaper one.
PRACTICAL: budget for up to 4N in the worst case, and expect roughly 2x on real game positions.
